feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and skills-heavy, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good use of scale and scope: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and analytics stack details add impact.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital leadership: combines strategy, CMS/web execution, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a convincing way.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily; consolidate to create a tighter, more executive-level CV.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities. Several bullets describe what you led, but fewer show measurable results such as growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, or cost/time savings.  
- Fix minor style/grammar inconsistencies: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less overlap with the competencies/skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Add a clearer senior-value proposition tied to recent work: enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and analytics-enabled communications for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Trim broad channel lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) to avoid repeating skills already covered elsewhere.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in enterprise web modernization, digital governance, content operations, and analytics-informed communications. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear public-facing content, aligning stakeholders, and creating scalable systems that improve execution across web, email, social, and multimedia.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and channel lists repeat content already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Workflows and systems” overlaps with multiple skills sections; keep the intro focused on positioning, not inventory.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it sharper and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and standardize style/plurals: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Prioritize strategic and leadership-oriented items over generic ones; e.g., replace “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” with “Cross-functional leadership & stakeholder engagement.”
- Reduce overlap with detailed technical sections by keeping this block high level and outcome-oriented.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Content operations & systems architecture • Cross-functional leadership & stakeholder engagement • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “policy & advocacy communication,” and coordination language repeat the header and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory scope, platform delivery, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and cross-channel governance as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one outcome-focused line: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make delivery bullets more active and specific: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, campaign launches, search improvement metrics, or efficiency gains from AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, and coordinated communications” overlaps with the Director and Associate Director entries; keep this item focused on consulting/advisory impact.
- The AI search and microsite work also appears in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-value leadership entry with solid scale signals; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish strategic ownership from the more operational NACo roles before and after it. The website migration and analytics buildout are the strongest proof points.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible for email/social/video/analytics: growth %, engagement lift, production savings, reporting speed, campaign performance, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Tighten wording and reduce platform lists unless tied to a result: “Built analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/publishing standards/workflows” overlaps with the current consultant role and Associate Director entry; keep this version at the enterprise/leadership level.
- Video channel development overlaps with earlier NACo roles; frame this as scaling in-house studio capacity, not launching video.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and process improvements before the higher-level strategic scope of 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, audience growth, publishing volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine the last two bullets for concision: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Established video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role’s “weekly video updates.”
- “Editorial coordination/workflows” also overlaps with the 2022–2024 role’s governance and planning systems.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad labels with sharper, executive-level language tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing operations & content systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy, information architecture & campaign planning
- Use “communications” or “content strategy” consistently; avoid mixing “messaging,” “planning,” and “leadership” without clear distinction.
- If space allows elsewhere, move proof points like “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views” into experience only, not skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already well evidenced in multiple NACo roles; keep it concise here.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your NACo work: platform modernization, implementation, automation, and AI/search.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from software list to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Drop or de-emphasize older/less central items like jQuery unless specifically required for target roles.
- Consider replacing “Power Pages”/“SharePoint” with “enterprise web platforms” if those tools are not featured in recent experience.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “AI-enabled search initiative” elsewhere in experience, not here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve exact tools for the technical section.
- “CMS modernization” also overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Web & CMS administration.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for your most recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around decision-making impact and avoid repeating “analytics & reporting” language already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome, e.g.:

- KPI framework design and executive dashboard reporting
- Web performance, user behavior, and conversion analysis
- SEO insights and optimization planning
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboard reporting” or “Executive-ready performance reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented term such as “measurement strategy,” “decision support,” or “insight generation.”
- Keep this section concise; the detailed platform expansion already appears in the Director of Digital Media role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with broader “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies.
- Tool names duplicate the 2022–2024 role; this skills item should summarize, not restate that bullet.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a duplicate of “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either be more concise or add context on level of use, with emphasis on Drupal given the recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and prioritize by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Better option: add proficiency context, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise CMS migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, group by strength: “Primary: Drupal, WordPress | Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a specific achievement or portfolio example; it feels lighter than the other platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Topline Skills → “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same wording elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more specific, e.g. “Front-End & Technical Implementation.”
- Tighten and modernize the list: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they date the section without adding value.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “for Drupal/CMS builds, analytics tagging, automation, and deployment workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations.” Consider removing those from one section.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions/Cloudflare Workers if described elsewhere.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already present in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize application, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**.
- Trim to the most relevant systems and group by function: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana • Slack/Teams**.
- If accurate, add a short qualifier instead of a pure list: **Built and managed workflow automation, editorial planning, and cross-team coordination systems using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, and Teams.**
- Drop older/lower-signal tools unless they are job-relevant for the target role: **Basecamp, Trello**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim here.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar project-management tools; listing all four can dilute impact.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the level of ownership implied by the recent NACo roles. Tightening the label and ordering by strongest/recently used platforms would make it feel more intentional.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope words instead of just names: **Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- Keep this item platform-specific; let the work experience carry outcomes like audience size, newsletter volume, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email” is already emphasized repeatedly in the summary and NACo roles, so avoid adding generic phrases like “email marketing” unless tied to platform specialization.
- Don’t repeat analytics or workflow language here; those are already covered in other Technical + IT and Topline Skills sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams/videos produced, newsletter cadence, or audience growth.
- Tighten the second sentence around distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate’s daily work.”
- If possible, add one outcome phrase: “improving publishing consistency, production capacity, or audience engagement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or piloting the format here.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; position this as the initial buildout rather than ongoing optimization.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy communications.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy, member engagement, or program visibility.
- Consider splitting into 2 bullets for readability if the CV format allows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research coordination + first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in later, more senior NACo roles.
